context: Set theory: Kuratowski realization with coordinatewise equality
text: For arbitrary sets a and b, the Kuratowski ordered pair is (a,b):={{a},{a,b}}. This set-theoretic construction has the defining property (a,b)=(c,d) if and only if a=c and b=d.
mathematical_review_note: The ProofWiki source explicitly provides the Kuratowski realization. It is a rigorous implementation of ordered coordinates in ZF-style set theory. Alternative Wiener or empty-set-based encodings can satisfy the same pair equality criterion but are not literally the same set.
variant_label: Kuratowski realization; alternative encodings held as separate variant leads

context: Set theory: non-strict subset relation for sets
text: For sets A and B, A is a subset of B, written A⊆B, if and only if for every x, x∈A implies x∈B. Equality A=B is allowed in this non-strict inclusion relation.
mathematical_review_note: ProofWiki's subset page gives the universal membership criterion and uses non-strict ⊆. The separate strict variant requires inequality; treating ⊆ as universally strict would be mathematically incorrect and conflict with common conventions.

context: Set theory: strict set inclusion requiring inequality
text: For sets A and B, A is a proper subset of B, written A⊊B, if and only if A⊆B and A≠B. Equivalently, every member of A belongs to B and at least one member of B does not belong to A.
mathematical_review_note: This stricter relation is sourced from the independently examined subset/proper-subset distinction. Unlike the ordinary subset relation, proper subset never permits A=B; it is not a second meaning for the same non-strict symbol.
variant_label: Proper subset is a distinct mathematical term

context: Foundational mapping as total single-valued assignment X→Y
text: Given sets X and Y, a mapping f:X→Y assigns to every x∈X exactly one value f(x)∈Y. Equivalently, for each x∈X there exists a unique y∈Y that the assignment associates with x.
mathematical_review_note: ProofWiki Mapping Definition 1 is total and single-valued. This pedagogically earlier element-assignment formulation keeps X as the full domain, Y as the specified codomain, and excludes partial or multivalued assignments.

text: For sets X and Y, a mapping f:X→Y can be defined as a typed relation (X,Y,G) where G⊆X×Y and, for every x∈X, there exists exactly one y∈Y with (x,y)∈G. The graph is G; X and Y are part of the mapping data.
mathematical_review_note: ProofWiki Mapping Definition 2 gives a typed relation and the two conditions existence and uniqueness. This form is equivalent to total single-valued assignment when domains and codomains are fixed but differs as an object from a bare subset.

context: Graph-only function convention relative to specified sets X,Y
text: With ambient sets X and Y fixed, a graph-only mapping can be represented by a subset G⊆X×Y such that, for every x∈X, there is exactly one y∈Y with (x,y)∈G. As bare data G need not determine the codomain Y uniquely.
mathematical_review_note: This source-dependent bare-subset representation is valid only with specified ambient X and Y and a totality/uniqueness condition. It must not be identified as literally the same typed object as (X,Y,G), especially when distinct codomains contain the same image.
variant_label: Context-limited bare-graph formulation, not synonymous as typed objects
